content:
In recent years, Macs have become increasingly popular and more affordable. The starting price has dropped, you get more RAM and storage for your money, and with the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple has for the first time become one of the best value options on the market.

Unfortunately, due to the ongoing memory shortage, Apple has significantly raised prices. Macs are no longer as attractive as before, but if you need a new computer, compared to other products on the market, I'd still say a Mac is a decent choice.

MacBook Air

Before the MacBook Neo launched, the MacBook Air was the entry-level option in Apple's laptop lineup. Although the MacBook Neo has made its value proposition a bit awkward, I still believe that if you're looking for a better user experience and don't need any high-end features, the MacBook Air is an excellent laptop.

MagSafe magnetic charging, P3 wide colour gamut display, Center Stage video calling, and longer battery life are just some of the highlights of the MacBook Air. It also comes in a 15-inch version, while the MacBook Neo is only available in 13 inches.

MacBook Neo

This product needs little introduction — the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordably priced MacBook, starting at just $699.

Compared to the MacBook Air mentioned above, it has some trade-offs, but at this price point, it's still an excellent value choice. Build quality, display clarity, and the macOS experience are essentially uncompromised. Of course, you'll need to accept the slower A18 Pro chip (but honestly, performance is by no means poor), fewer ports, and only 8GB of RAM, but at this price it's completely reasonable. It also comes in several fun colours, such as citrus yellow, pink, and indigo.

Currently the MacBook Neo doesn't have many substantial retail discounts, but Apple offers refurbished versions at $100 to $120 off the original price. Apple certified refurbished products come with a one-year warranty, look like new, have all major components replaced, and won't have any scratches or battery wear issues.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $689 at Amazon ($10 off)

  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $599 at Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $679 at Apple Store

MacBook Pro

The MacBook Pro is the top-tier model in the lineup. You can get the most cutting-edge configurations, but there's one thing to note. Reports indicate Apple will redesign the high-end MacBook Pro later this year, with an OLED display, touch functionality, and a thinner chassis.

However, this redesign will only debut alongside the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips — so if you're buying the entry-level model with the M5 chip, there's no problem at all with buying a new MacBook now. Even if you don't care about the redesign at all, the M5 Pro and M5 Max themselves are already quite impressive new chips.
